original_text: Encapsulating ML Models within Rule-based Safeguards

It is impossible to guarantee the correctness of ML model predictions, so they should not be directly used for safety- or security-related functions. Furthermore, ML models can be unstable and vulnerable to adversarial attacks, data noise, and drift.
Introduce a deterministic, rule-based mechanism that decides what to do with the prediction results, e.g., based on additional quality checks.
Reduced risk for negative impacts of incorrect predictions, but a more complex architecture.
Document-Grounded Response Safeguards
Proposed

Store attendants need procedural guidance for handling customer requests. The system must answer according to the company's official documents and state that it cannot help when no document contains guidance for the procedure. AI-produced responses may not always satisfy these conditions, so the architecture must prevent unsupported guidance from reaching attendants.

We will place a deterministic, rule-based safeguard between AI-produced guidance and its delivery to store attendants. The safeguard will allow a response only when it is consistent with guidance in the company's official documents. If no official document contains guidance for the requested procedure, the system will tell the attendant that it cannot help.

This will reduce the risk of attendants receiving unsupported procedural guidance, though it cannot guarantee that every permitted answer is correct. The safeguard adds architectural complexity and may prevent a response from being delivered when the AI-produced guidance does not meet its rules.
Partial Rejection of Safety Responsibility

Recent developments in ML and DL allowed probabilistic systems with large input and output spaces to be explored in safety critical systems. This introduces safety-related challenges, such as: (1) Model complexity and opacity, (2) Dealing with probabilistic output, (3) Sensitivity to distribution shifts (4) Formal verification is impossible or not scalable and more. This safety responsibility has to be dealt with.
A system decides to reject the predictions of a DL algorith or delay any decisions until it is confident enough
One can allow some uncertainty in a system, while imposing relatively low constraints on the DL algorithms used.
Rejection of Unsupported Procedural Answers
Proposed

Store attendants need guidance on how to handle customer requests. The system must answer according to the company’s official documents and inform the attendant when no document contains guidance for the requested procedure. The architecture must therefore account for requests that lack a documented answer.

We will reject a proposed procedural answer when the company’s official documents do not support it. If no document contains guidance for the requested procedure, we will tell the attendant that the system cannot help rather than provide an unsupported answer.

Attendants will not receive procedural guidance that lacks support in the official documents. Requests without documented guidance will remain unanswered, so the system’s ability to help depends on the guidance those documents contain.

To control prediction with parameter.
When it is possible to control rule-based.

Add a mechanism in your code to change behaviour of all or a part of the predictions, including stopping, retrying or timeout. Since it is difficult to keep high accuracy without any error for a model for every case or every input data, it is better to estimate possible anomaly and control with rulebased mechanism.

Pros: avoid abnormal prediction for edge cases.

Document-Grounded Response Control
Proposed

Store attendants need answers about how to handle customer requests. The system must answer in accordance with official company documents and must say that it cannot help when no document contains guidance for the procedure. The architecture therefore needs to control when it provides procedural guidance.

We will apply a rule-based control to procedural responses. We will provide guidance only when an official company document contains guidance for the procedure, and we will keep the response consistent with that document. When no document contains such guidance, we will withhold procedural guidance and tell the attendant that the system cannot help.

This control reduces the risk of giving attendants procedural advice unsupported by official documents. Its effectiveness depends on correctly determining whether the documents contain applicable guidance. The control cannot account for every case, and additional rules may increase operational complexity.

Integração cliente-servidor para registro de chamados
Proposed

O atendimento de primeiro nível de TI abrange solicitações como bloqueio de sites e instalação de softwares. O sistema deve responder a procedimentos e dúvidas sobre o portfólio de serviços de TI e documentar as solicitações por meio de integração com o sistema de chamados. Essa integração exige definir qual sistema solicita o registro e qual presta esse serviço.

Vamos estabelecer uma relação cliente-servidor para o registro de chamados. O sistema de suporte atuará como cliente e iniciará solicitações ao sistema de chamados, que atuará como servidor e prestará o serviço de registro para documentar as solicitações dos usuários.

O registro dos chamados ficará centralizado no sistema de chamados. Em contrapartida, a documentação das solicitações dependerá da disponibilidade desse sistema, e a operação do serviço de registro exigirá gestão. Essa integração não define como o sistema responderá às dúvidas e aos procedimentos do portfólio de TI.

Rule-Based Safeguards for Catalog-Grounded Answers
Proposed

The multi-area support system must show all sources used in an answer, identifying the document, version, and section of each retrieved passage. Answers must contain only information from the company catalog. Because AI-generated content may not reliably meet these conditions, the architecture needs a way to check answers before presenting them.

We will place deterministic, rule-based checks between answer generation and presentation. These checks will allow only content supported by retrieved passages from the company catalog and will require the answer to show every source used, with its document, version, and section. The system will withhold content that does not meet these checks.

Presented answers will be more traceable to the company catalog, reducing the risk of unsupported information. The checks will add architectural complexity and may prevent some content from being shown when catalog support or the required source details cannot be established.
Fluid Architecture

Classical architecture and UX patterns, though largely successful, suffer the following limitations in AI contexts: (1) Static interfaces, (2) Lack of bidirectionality, (3) Slow updates, (4) subiptimal personalization, (5) interpretability and explainability

Additional to any AI that runs in a backend, there is an AI in the frontend to evolve the interface and adapt it to changes. Moreover, there is an AI orchestrator. Its purposes are to monitor the performance of both the frontend’s AI and the backend’s AI to make sure that their respective performance is satisfactory and to witness contract negotiations to see how the interactions between the frontend and backend evolve over time.
The aforementioned limitations are alleviated.
Adaptive Presentation of Answer Sources
Proposed

Users need to see every source used in a requested answer, including the document, version, and section of each retrieved passage. The system must report only information in the company catalog. The presentation of answers therefore needs to remain aligned with their source information.

We will establish a frontend AI that adapts the presentation of answers to show every source used and its document, version, and section. A backend AI will provide answers limited to the company catalog and the associated source information. An AI orchestrator will monitor both AI capabilities and oversee how their interaction evolves so that the presentation remains aligned with the answers and their sources.

Users will be able to see the catalog sources behind answers, making their origins easier to understand. The frontend and backend will need to keep answer content and source details aligned. The additional frontend AI and orchestrator will also introduce monitoring and coordination responsibilities.

Rule-Based Controls for Catalog Answers
Proposed

Users need to see all sources used in an answer, including the document, version, and section of each retrieved excerpt. Answers must report only information in the company catalog. The architecture therefore needs to control what information appears in answers while preserving the required source details.

We will apply rule-based controls to answers so that they report only content from the company catalog. For every retrieved excerpt used in an answer, we will show its document, version, and section; content that does not meet these conditions will not be reported.

Answers will be limited to catalog content, and users will be able to identify the sources used. Content without the required source details may have to be excluded. The controls cannot cover every possible erroneous answer, and maintaining more rules may increase operational complexity.

Staged Generation of Procurement Documents
Proposed

The system must generate an initial document based on a record in the procurement system. It must use the administrator-registered layout appropriate to the document type, replace layout variables with AI-generated content, and produce readable, harmonious text in technical-legal language. These requirements involve distinct transformations that must work together in the final document.

We will generate the document through a sequence of processing stages. The stages will select the appropriate registered layout, replace its variables with AI-generated content, and combine the layout and variable text into a readable, harmonious document in technical-legal language. Each stage will pass its result to the next.

Separating the transformations will make it easier to adjust one stage without changing the entire generation flow. The stages will also need to remain coordinated: a change to an intermediate result can affect the readability, formatting, or language of the final document.
Model-View-Controller (MVC)
The system is required to facilitate multiple views of the same data object and single view of multiple data objects.
Includes three parts: Model (internal data), View (data representation) and Controller (I/O Controller). Only the model layer should be altered.
This pattern greatly enhances the code reusability and system enpansibility.
Separate Document Content from Layout and Generation Control
Proposed

The system must generate an initial procurement document from a registered record. It must use the administrator-registered layout appropriate to the document type, replace layout variables with AI-generated content, and produce readable, coherent text in technical-legal language. These requirements distinguish the document content from its representation and from the handling of the generation request.

We will separate document generation into a model that holds the registered record and generated variable content, a view that represents the document using the appropriate registered layout, and a controller that coordinates the generation request and resulting document. The view will combine the layout text with substituted variable content to produce a readable, coherent document in the required technical-legal style.

Separating content from its representation will make it easier to reuse generation behavior across document types and their layouts. It will also require the model, view, and controller to remain coordinated as layouts and document types change. The completed text must still be checked for readability, coherence, and technical-legal language; the separation alone does not ensure those qualities.

Separação entre composição documental e geração por IA
Proposed

O documento inicial deve corresponder ao registro cadastrado no sistema de licitações, usar o layout apropriado ao tipo de documento e seguir o layout cadastrado pelo administrador. O conteúdo das variáveis será gerado pelo modelo de IA em linguagem técnico-jurídica, enquanto a substituição das variáveis e a composição do texto devem preservar a legibilidade e a harmonia do documento. Essas responsabilidades precisam permanecer distinguíveis.

We will separate the business logic that selects the registered layout, replaces variables, and composes the document from the AI model that generates the content for those variables. We will define a clear interface through which the generated content is provided for insertion into the appropriate layout, while preserving the required technical-legal language and a readable, harmonious result.

The layout and composition rules can be maintained separately from adjustments to AI-generated content. This separation makes it clearer which responsibility to address when the document does not meet its requirements. It also requires maintaining the interface between the two responsibilities; separating them does not, by itself, ensure that generated text follows the required language standard or fits harmoniously into the layout.

Separate Document Construction from Layout Representation
Proposed

The system must generate an initial bidding document based on a registered record. It must use the administrator-registered layout appropriate to the document type, replace layout variables with AI-generated content, and produce readable, harmonious text in technical-legal language. This requires the document’s content and layout to be brought together without treating them as the same concern.

We will separate construction of the initial document from its layout representation. The registered layout selected for the document type will define the representation, while document construction will replace its variables with AI-generated content and combine that content with the layout text into a readable, harmonious document in technical-legal language.

Layouts can vary by document type without being conflated with the AI-generated content used to fill them. Document construction must still account for the variables in each selected layout and ensure that the combined text remains coherent and follows the required language standard; separating construction from representation does not guarantee those qualities on its own.

When in your business logic, the model inference is a blocker to proceed to the next step
blocks the system's workflow until the prediction finishes

Easy to manage with its simplicity. All operational aspects like transaction tracing, monitoring etc become easy as well. Service workflow becomes simple for the process won't proceed until the prediction completes.
But: (1) The prediction latency can become a performance bottleneck.
(2) You might have to consider a workaround for not degrading your user experience because of prediction latency. (3) If the client of your service is another service then this pattern leads to blocked threads on the client side.
Synchronous Assembly of Initial Documents
Proposed

The system must generate an initial procurement document using the administrator-registered layout appropriate to its document type. It must replace layout variables with AI-generated content and combine the text in a readable, harmonious form using technical-legal language. Variable substitution and document assembly depend on the model completing its generation.

We will make the document-generation workflow wait for the AI model to finish generating variable content before replacing variables and combining that content with the appropriate registered layout. The workflow will not assemble the initial document until the generated content is available.

This keeps the sequence of generation and assembly straightforward and makes the workflow easier to trace and monitor. Model latency will delay completion of the document and may affect the user's experience.

Rule-Based Safeguards for Document Revisions
Proposed

The assistant must improve user-provided text, including corrections and adjustments to technical-legal conventions. It must also support previously standardized document types and allow users to rephrase, summarize, or expand content. These changes must preserve the context and purpose of the resulting artifact, while automated revisions may produce incorrect results.

We will place deterministic, rule-based safeguards between automated text revision and acceptance of the revised content. The safeguards will check proposed corrections, adjustments, rephrasings, summaries, and expansions against conditions for preserving the artifact’s context and purpose, and will prevent revisions that fail those checks from being applied.

The safeguards will reduce the risk of accepting revisions that change an artifact’s context or purpose, but they cannot guarantee that every accepted revision is correct. They will also make the architecture more complex and may prevent some acceptable revisions when those revisions fail the checks.

Context-Preserving Document Text Processing Pipeline
Proposed

Users need to improve text in standardized procurement documents by correcting errors and aligning wording with technical-legal norms. They also need to reformulate, summarize, or expand content without changing the context or purpose of the resulting artifact. These varied text-processing tasks need to work together across different standardized document types.

We will process document text through a sequence of separable transformation stages. The stages will perform correction, technical-legal adjustment, and the user-requested reformulation, summarization, or expansion as appropriate. Each stage will pass its result to the next while preserving the text’s context and the artifact’s purpose.

Separating the transformations will make it easier to modify or add text-processing steps than in a single, combined process. However, the stages will need to work together so that successive changes do not alter the document’s context or purpose.

Parameter-Controlled Document Transformation
Proposed

Users need to correct and adapt text to technical-legal norms across different types of previously standardized documents. They must be able to reformulate, summarize, or expand content while preserving the context and purpose of the resulting artifact. These transformation choices require control over the generated text, and an otherwise useful revision may be unacceptable if it changes the artifact’s meaning.

We will parameterize text transformation according to the user’s selected action—reformulate, summarize, or expand—and the document’s context and purpose. We will apply rule-based controls to the generated text and stop or retry a transformation when those controls identify a departure from that context or purpose.

Users can request different transformations while the system limits revisions that its rules identify as inconsistent with the artifact’s context or purpose. The controls cannot detect every problematic change, so they do not guarantee preservation in every case. Adding and maintaining rules will also increase operational complexity.

On-Demand Iterative Text Enrichment
Proposed

Users need to improve text in previously standardized document types by correcting errors and aligning it with technical-legal standards. They must also be able to request context-aware reformulations, summaries, and expansions without changing the context or purpose of the resulting artifact. A fixed, one-way editing process would not accommodate these successive requests.

We will structure text improvement as an automated, user-initiated, iterative enrichment cycle. For each request, the system will transform the supplied text according to the requested improvement and allow further reformulation, summarization, or expansion, while preserving the text’s context and the artifact’s purpose across supported document types.

Users can request improvements as needed and refine the result through successive transformations rather than relying on a single editing pass. Repeated transformations may make it harder to preserve the original context and purpose, particularly across different document types; each iteration must remain aligned with those requirements.

When prediction target varies a lot by condition. When you can conditionally select a model in a rule-based manner.
Deploy various models and define selection rules for them. Depending on certain attributes of the input data, the most adequate model is used.

Positive: Select an adequate model depending on condition.
Negative: Operational cost raise with number of models.
Conditional Model Selection for Document Text Improvement
Proposed

Users need to improve text in standardized procurement documents by correcting errors and aligning it with technical-legal norms. The system must preserve the artifact’s context and purpose while supporting three different requested outcomes: rephrasing, summarizing, and expanding content. The expected result therefore varies with the user’s requested operation.

We will make multiple text-improvement models available and establish rules that select a model according to whether the user requests rephrasing, summarization, or expansion. The selected model will process the text in its document context, with the goal of correcting errors and meeting the applicable technical-legal norm without changing the artifact’s context or purpose.

Selection by requested operation allows the system to direct each text-improvement task to an appropriate model. Operating multiple models increases cost, and the selection rules must be maintained. Model selection alone does not guarantee that an edited text preserves the artifact’s context and purpose.

Staged Processing for Saving the Complete Document
Proposed

When a user saves a document, the system must compile all its parts, correct any grammatical errors in the saved version, and inform the user which words were corrected. These distinct tasks must produce a consistent saved document and correction report.

We will process the document through sequential stages that compile its parts, correct grammatical errors while retaining which words changed, and then save the corrected document and report the corrected words to the user.

Separating the tasks makes individual stages easier to modify than a single combined operation. The stages must remain in order, and correction information must be carried forward so the reported words correspond to the saved version.

Separate Document Assembly from the Saved Document
Proposed

The user needs to save a complete bidding document assembled from all its parts. The saved version must have grammatical errors corrected, and the user must be told which words were corrected. These requirements call for a way to construct the complete document while keeping the reported corrections consistent with the saved version.

We will separate construction of the complete document from its saved representation. The construction process will compile all document parts, produce the grammatically corrected version for saving, and identify the corrected words to report to the user.

The saved document will contain all compiled parts and the grammatical corrections, with the corrected words available to report to the user. Separating construction from the saved representation introduces an assembly step and requires the reported corrections to remain consistent with the version that is saved.

Proposed

The AI system must receive all images submitted by the customer and verify whether the document photo belongs to the customer who submitted the selfie. An incorrect AI assessment could undermine this identity check. Because AI predictions cannot be guaranteed correct, the architecture must account for that uncertainty when determining the verification outcome.

The safeguards will determine how to handle the assessment result, so the AI prediction alone will not decide whether the document photo belongs to the customer.

Salvaguardas por regras para a alteração do status do atendimento
Proposed

A confirmação pela IA de que o documento pertence ao cliente desencadeia a alteração do status do atendimento para PENDENTE DE EXECUÇÃO. Essa alteração leva o sistema Comercial a comunicar o cliente e a seguir com a programação do atendimento. Como uma confirmação incorreta pode liberar essas etapas indevidamente, a arquitetura precisa controlar quando o resultado da IA pode produzir a mudança de status.

We will submeter o resultado da confirmação de titularidade feita pela IA a uma decisão determinística baseada em regras antes de solicitar ao sistema Comercial a alteração do status para PENDENTE DE EXECUÇÃO. Somente um resultado autorizado por essas regras poderá desencadear a mudança de status; um resultado não autorizado não a desencadeará.

A decisão reduz o risco de que uma confirmação incorreta da IA provoque a comunicação ao cliente e a programação do atendimento. A comunicação e a programação permanecem vinculadas à mudança de status no sistema Comercial. Em contrapartida, a verificação por regras acrescenta complexidade à arquitetura e não elimina a possibilidade de erros na confirmação.

Proposed

The Commercial system will perform the change, notify the customer, and continue scheduling the service.

Proposed

When the AI system confirms that a document belongs to the customer, it must change the service status in the Commercial system to PENDENTE DE EXECUÇÃO. That status change enables the Commercial system to notify the customer and proceed with scheduling. When the AI system confirms that a document belongs to the customer, it must change the service request’s status in the company’s Commercial system to PENDENTE DE EXECUÇÃO. Synchronous Document Validation Before Status Change
Proposed

The AI system must confirm that a document belongs to the customer before changing the service request status. The Commercial system’s customer notification and service scheduling depend on that status change, so the workflow must not advance before validation is complete.

We will hold the service request workflow until the AI system completes document validation. When validation confirms that the document belongs to the customer, the AI system will communicate with the Commercial system to change the status to PENDENTE DE EXECUÇÃO, allowing the Commercial system to notify the customer and proceed with scheduling.

The workflow will preserve the required order between validation, status change, notification, and scheduling. This sequence is straightforward to follow, but validation latency can delay the status change and all subsequent steps.

Proposed

When the AI system confirms that a submitted document does not belong to the customer, it must mark the service as improcedente and record the reason in the company's Commercial system. The Commercial system must then notify the customer. The architecture needs to define how the AI system requests this update while leaving notification with the Commercial system.

Rule-Based Safeguards for Model Evaluation
Proposed

Data scientists and control engineers need to evaluate control and AI model recommendations in the digital twin before applying them to the real ETA. Models must receive the variables expected in the real environment, but their commands and recommendations may be applied only in simulation. Each execution must be recorded, and different models must be comparable under the same scenario. Because model outputs cannot be assumed to be correct, the architecture needs to preserve the boundary between evaluation and real operation.

We will place a deterministic, rule-based safeguard between connected models and the application of their commands or recommendations. The safeguard will permit those outputs to affect only the simulated environment and prevent their application to the real ETA. Guarded evaluations will provide models with the variables expected in the real environment and record each execution's inputs, outputs, and results so that different models can be compared under the same scenario.

Model outputs can be evaluated without directly affecting the real ETA, reducing the risk from incorrect recommendations. Recorded executions and shared scenarios support model comparison. The safeguard adds architectural complexity, and its rules must remain consistent with the simulation-only boundary.

Separate Models from Digital Twin Simulation and Evaluation
Proposed

Data scientists and control engineers need to connect control and AI models to the digital twin to assess their recommendations before applying them in the real ETA. Models must receive the variables planned for the real environment, while their commands or recommendations must affect only the simulation. Each execution must be recorded, and different models must be comparable under the same scenario. These needs call for a clear boundary between model behavior and the twin’s simulation and evaluation functions.

We will separate simulation, connected models, and execution evaluation into three layers with explicit interfaces between the models and the other functions. The simulation layer will supply the required variables and apply model commands or recommendations only in the simulated environment. The evaluation layer will record each execution’s inputs, outputs, and results and support comparison of different models using the same scenario. Data will flow separately from the simulation to the models as inputs, from the models to the simulation as commands or recommendations, and from executions to evaluation as recorded results.

Models can be changed and compared without combining their behavior with the twin’s simulation and evaluation responsibilities. Recorded executions will make their recommendations and results available for assessment before use in the real ETA. The separation also requires maintaining the interfaces and coordinating the three data flows so that models receive consistent variables and comparisons use the same scenario.
